sections.h2: What should a Bedford, TX owner weigh before a quick sale?
sections.html:
Bedford is a small, fully built suburb in northeast Tarrant County, and a house there is usually sold into a crowded metro market. Owners deal with Tarrant Appraisal District paperwork, a city rental registry and buyers who commute across the Metroplex.

The Census Bureau estimated 47,958 residents for mid-2025, a 4.0% drop from the April 2020 estimates base. With roughly half of homes rented, a seller may be dealing with tenants, a registration file and a tax ceiling transfer all at once.

sections.h2: Where is Bedford, and what is it like to live there?
sections.html:
According to the city's economic development page, Bedford lies in northeast Tarrant County along SH-121, about 14 miles from downtown Fort Worth and 22 miles from downtown Dallas. The page also puts DFW International Airport within five miles and Dallas Love Field 22 miles away.

The city covers roughly 10 square miles, or 6,393 acres, and describes itself as a suburb with a solid base of medical providers, small businesses, national retailers and restaurants. Its partnership with the Hurst-Euless-Bedford Chamber of Commerce helps with business recruitment.

  • 14 miles from downtown Fort Worth, 22 from downtown Dallas
  • Five miles from DFW International Airport
  • Medical, retail and restaurant employers inside the city
  • Economic development work shared with the Hurst-Euless-Bedford Chamber of Commerce

sections.h2: How did Bedford grow from a ranch town to a suburb?
sections.html:
The city's own park history says Bedford voted to incorporate on January 22, 1953, partly out of worry about being absorbed by Euless or Hurst. It then had a little over 400 residents in a two-square-mile area.

The Variety Club of Dallas ran the Bedford Boys Ranch on 232 acres from 1949 to 1957. The city optioned a 52.6 acre tract in 1973, and it became Bedford Boys Ranch Park on July 6, 1974. The senior center followed in 1976 and the outdoor aquatic center, Splash, in 2003. A 2009 round of work, costing $3.2 million, added pedestrian bridges, a playground, disc golf, fishing piers and trails. Homes near that park are a natural selling point.

sections.h2: How do Bedford housing figures compare with other Texas suburbs?
sections.html:
The 2020-2024 survey puts the midpoint owner-occupied home in Bedford at $350,700, and owners live in 50.6% of units. Renters pay a midpoint of $1,502 a month.

The city fits 10.03 square miles of land, and the 2020 count shows 4,977.9 residents per square mile. The average trip to a job runs 24.5 minutes, and 43.5% of residents past age 24 hold a four-year degree.

sections.h2: What exemptions does the Tarrant Appraisal District offer Bedford homeowners?
sections.html:
Tarrant Appraisal District handles homestead exemption applications, and its page says there is no fee to file. Owners can submit online, by mail, or at the office on Handley-Ederville Road in Fort Worth.

  • Residential homestead for owners who live in the house
  • Over-65 and disabled exemptions, which also bring a ceiling on school and locally adopted city, county and special district taxes
  • Disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions based on the service-connected rating
  • Heir owners may claim the homestead on the whole property, not a share

Owners who are 65 or older, disabled or disabled veterans can also defer paying the homestead tax while it keeps accruing. A homeowner whose value rose by more than 5% over the prior year may defer the extra portion as well. Interest runs at 8% per year, and the deferred tax stays a lien on the property.

sections.h2: How much can a Bedford tax bill grow in a year?
sections.html:
Texas shields a homestead with a $140,000 school exemption and adds $60,000 for older or disabled owners. Each taxing unit may add its own percentage exemption on top.

Assessed homestead value may climb only 10% a year once the first full year of exemption has passed. Bills go out around October 1, and a six percent penalty plus one percent interest begins on February 1 for unpaid balances. Some collectors allow a delinquent homestead owner to pay over as many as 36 months.

Yes. Owners must register with the city before renting a home for fewer than 29 days at a time, and no property is exempt from the requirement.

Short-term rentals are only allowed in residential zoning, not in multi-family districts, and none may sit within 1,000 feet of another registered short-term rental. The city requires an annual fire inspection, a repeat inspection if problems appear, and a new inspection on a change of ownership.

  • Host liability insurance with the city named as additional insured
  • Proof that property taxes are current
  • House rules covering occupancy limits, off-street parking, quiet hours and a 24-hour local contact
  • A dimensioned floorplan showing emergency exits

Hotel occupancy tax is due monthly by the 20th for the prior month, and a report is required even when no stays occurred. A buyer who plans a rental should ask Neighborhood Services how a sale affects the registration.

sections.h2: What timeline does a lender follow on a Bedford foreclosure?
sections.html:
Deeds of trust in Tarrant County typically give the lender a power of sale, so the house goes to auction without a lawsuit. Sales happen on a first Tuesday, and the notice sets a start time that may not slip more than three hours.

A default notice comes first, and the owner has 20 days from receiving it to pay what is past due. The sale notice then follows with at least 21 days to spare. If the lender wants the leftover balance after the sale, it must sue within two years.

sections.h2: How does an inherited Bedford house move to a buyer?
sections.html:
Start the probate of a will inside four years after the death, in the probate court of the county where the person lived. Where debts are limited to liens on real estate, a muniment of title lets the court order and the will carry title.

The paper a title company wants depends on the route taken. A transfer on death deed pairs with an affidavit of death and a certificate, an administered estate relies on an executor's or administrator's deed, and an uncontested will with no administration relies on the court order. The county cannot add heirs to the old deed on its own.

sections.h2: Where does a Bedford deed get filed?
sections.html:
Tarrant County's clerk files the deed, because Texas keeps deed records in the county where the land sits. A conveyance needs a signature and either a notary's acknowledgment or two witnesses.

The state clerk manual lists $5.00 for page one and $4.00 per added page, with other clerk fees on top. Confirm the total with the Tarrant County Clerk before you mail a deed.

faqs.q: What is a house in Bedford worth?
faqs.a: The 2020-2024 survey midpoint for owner-occupied homes is $350,700. Condition, lot and street shift that figure, so rely on a written offer or an appraisal for your own house.

faqs.q: Can I list my Bedford house on Airbnb or Vrbo?
faqs.a: Only after registering with the city. Bedford requires registration and yearly inspection for stays under 29 days, and a short-term rental cannot sit within 1,000 feet of another.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to claim a homestead exemption in Bedford?
faqs.a: No. Tarrant Appraisal District says exemptions carry no fee, and most homestead applications are due by April 30.

faqs.q: Can a senior in Bedford postpone property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners over 65, disabled owners and disabled veterans may defer homestead tax, which keeps accruing at 8% interest per year and stays a lien on the house.

faqs.q: What paperwork finishes a Bedford sale?
faqs.a: A signed, acknowledged deed filed with the Tarrant County Clerk. A house that came from an estate may also need an affidavit of death, a court order or an executor's deed.
